t: The kingdom of the West Saxons, centred on Winchester, which grew from small beginnings in the upper Thames valley and the Solent region.
Under Alfred the Great it alone of the English kingdoms survived the Viking onslaught, defended by a network of fortified burhs.
Alfred’s heirs conquered the Danelaw, and in 927 Æthelstan made Wessex the core of the Kingdom of England.
dyk: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, first compiled in Wessex in Alfred’s reign, was still being kept up at Peterborough Abbey in 1154.
ev: Ceawlin wins the Battle of Dyrham, taking Gloucester, Cirencester and Bath
King Cynegils is baptised by Bishop Birinus
Ine issues the first West Saxon law code
Ecgberht defeats Mercia at the Battle of Ellendun
Alfred defeats Guthrum at the Battle of Edington
Alfred occupies London and is recognised as king of the Anglo-Saxons
Æthelstan takes York and becomes king of the English
